_meta.task: tier amendment 01 — corrections found by blind re-sampling
_meta.apply: run apply_tier_patch.py with this file AFTER TIER_PATCH_ALL.json; same schema, same script
_meta.finding: a national association OF local governments is national, not the tier of its members. Brazil's national confederation of municipalities was already filed national; the same body type in eleven other countries was filed at member level. Inter-municipal bodies (commonwealths, mancomunidades, consorcios, joint boards) are NOT in this class and are unchanged — their own jurisdiction really is the member territories.
_meta.also: two single corrections from the 130-row sample: a village-association movement filed national, and a national body filed international on a regional reach.
_meta.was_field: 'was' records the superseded value; it is metadata for review and is ignored by the applier
_meta.provenance: 12 rows from a name sweep for the association-of-local-governments class; 4 rows from two independent blind re-reads of 130-row stratified samples. Two of the four (TUR, COM) were in classes the sweep should have caught and did not — the sampling is what found them, which is the argument for keeping both methods.

rows.name: Mexico's national and regional municipal associations - technical support to ELABORATE AND REVIEW THE TECHNICAL FILES a council needs to request public money, donations and tenders, plus a joint national conference and state-level associations

Peru's rural municipalities network - joint and personalised technical accompaniment for small district councils, dialogue spaces open to non-governmental institutions, a water resources guide for local governments, and a national annual conference

Paraguay's association of municipal boards, association of departmental boards, council of governors and women officeholders' network - with an NGO that has trained councillors on budget scrutiny, and an honest warning about the inter-municipal organisation

Colombia's federation of municipalities - a TERRITORIAL ORDERING SERVICE of urbanistic, environmental and legal experts for less than one consultant's fee, three-day training open to actors the mayor designates, a weekly legal bulletin and a threatened-mayors protection programme

Bolivia's municipal associative system - a federation of 300+ municipalities with its own legal personality, nine departmental associations, a multidisciplinary technical team, and a learning network where NGOs may publish training for town halls

Chile's municipalities' association - MODEL ORDINANCES and studies for all 346 councils, a standing environment commission of mayors and councillors, regional associations in every region, and state help to give a multi-municipality association legal personality

Panama's municipalities' association and its framework agreement with a conservation organisation for CREATION OF DISTRICT PROTECTED AREAS in all 81 districts, plus staffed municipal environment directorates and the legal map of municipal protection agreements

Costa Rica's union of local governments - a public-law body with a NATIONAL DATABASE OF MUNICIPAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGERS and a technical network, chairing the municipal ecological flag committee, alongside regional federations of municipalities
Communities association and inter-community unions — the municipalities' own membership body, chaired by a mayor

Argentina's municipal climate network - free consultancies that produced DRAFT ORDINANCES for councils, technical accompaniment for local plans, pooled network financing for small communes, and a green jobs mapping programme

Ecuador's associations of provinces, municipalities and rural parishes - free technical assistance including drafting LOCAL CONSERVATION NORMATIVE, provincial offices that expedite parish procedures, and parish representatives elected onto provincial councils
Kyrgyz Jayity — the national association of the pasture committees that actually hold the land-use right

The village Ulanga movement — associations called Nature founded in most Comorian villages on two islands — plus Malezi Mema's first permanent community marine reserve, the Mrémani seedling nursery and 950 metres of anti-erosion lines
Environmental Defenders Office (EDO) — public-interest environmental law
Union of 480 municipalities for historic towns — dues turned back into conservation grants, and a competition open to a whole settlement

Research agencies that work on behalf of communities harmed by environmental violence and build evidence for courtrooms — 100+ investigations in 31 countries, plus a completed African partnership whose evidence communities can use in a reparations claim
